thread:
Alex: Quick heads-up — our canary (v2.3.1) was supposed to get 10% traffic but telemetry shows ~7% over the last 2 hours. Not a huge gap but enough to bias the A/B. Anyone seeing routing quirks?

Jia: saw that as well in the dashboard. The traffic-split metric under "rollouts" is reporting 10/90 but the event counts disagree.

Marco: is that based on frontend assignment or downstream routing? Could be sticky session + cookie expiry.

Sara: I pulled raw assignment events from the assignment service:
```
select variant, count(*) from assignments where rollout_id='canary-2026-03' and ts > now() - interval '3 hours' group by variant;
```
Result: A: 92,345 (93%), B: 6,982 (7%)

Alex: @Sara thanks. That matches the observation. The SDK returns assignedVariant consistently though.

Eva: ops-metrics shows a spike in 429s on the gateway around the canary start time — maybe gateway retries cause some requests to be rerouted to default pool which always hits control variant?

Marco: good catch. If gateway-level quota fallback points to dedicated pool running the control, that explains lower B. Check routing rules for quota fallback.

Samir: I can repro locally by forcing a 503 from the canary pool; our fallback path reassigns to the default model and doesn't re-emit assignment event for the original request. So assignment telemetry undercounts failed-to-canary traffic.

Jia: so two sources: (1) quota/fallback reassignments, (2) sticky sessions/cookies? Which is bigger?

Sara: looking at session cookie churn — not much. The counts where gateway returned 5xx and we retried to control align with the missing ~3% traffic.

Alex: important question: do we stop the A/B test? With a sample ratio mismatch (SRM) we risk invalid stats. Thoughts on remedy and whether to abort.

Marco: we should NOT rush to declare significance. Options: pause and fix routing so assignment telemetry equals actual exposure, then resume; or use IPW (inverse probability weighting) to adjust stats for observed exposure. But IPW assumes we can correctly estimate assignment probability per request.

Samir: I don't love IPW here because the retry logic is conditional on error states that might be correlated with variant. If fallback disproportionately affects B (the new model), IPW may still be biased.

Eva: operational fix first: disable automatic fallback to control for this rollout (set fallback_policy=fail-fast) and re-run canary for an extended window. We can also increase canary to 20% to get quicker stats after fix.

Jia: increasing to 20% is a policy change — needs product sign-off (but makes sense if we have confidence). Also need to update the console to show "observed assignment" vs "configured split" so folks don't get fooled.

Alex: agree on console change. Action items: (1) Ops: toggle fallback policy for this rollout to fail-fast (Samir + Eva), (2) Eng-platform: add observed-assignment metric in rollout dashboard (Marco + Jia), (3) Data: re-evaluate significance using only requests that were actually served by assigned variant (Sara).

Marco: timeline? I can add an "observed split" badge to the rollout console in ~3 hours if nothing blocks.

Samir: I'll open a rollback toggle and set fallback to fail-fast now in staging, then push to prod after smoke. ops-bot, can you create a ticket?

Ops-bot: Ticket created: RP-4271 "Canary 2026-03: investigate assignment mismatch & disable fallback". Assigned to Samir, Eva, Marco. Priority: P1. Link: https://redwoodinc.atlassian.net/browse/RP-4271 :white_check_mark:

Sara: For the stat analysis, I think we should hold off on hypothesis tests until we've fixed assignment or at least use only non-fallbacked requests. I'll extract a clean cohort. If we exclude fallbacked requests the sample size drops — might need to extend test duration.

Alex: OK. Decision: pause new decisions on promotion. Keep the canary live, but with fail-fast fallback and extended duration (+48h) or until we reach N=50k per variant (whichever later). Marco/Jia please prioritize dashboard change so "configured split" vs "observed" is visible in the top-level rollout card.

Marco: noted. Also proposing automatic SRM detector: if observed split deviates >2% absolute for >30m, flag and pause rollout. Should we add?

Jia: yes — and include a reason code (quota-fallback, sticky-session, gateway-errors) so runbooks are actionable.

Samir: after we fix routing, let's re-run the analysis and use bootstrap CIs rather than raw p-values — more robust to weird distributions.

Eva: rolling the fail-fast change to prod now. Will monitor errors closely and revert if anything unexpected.

Ops-bot: prod deploy started by Samir at 1754302010.

Eva: prod smoke looks good, no surge in 500s from canary. Observed split climbing: now 9.1% B over the last 15m.

Alex: good sign. Keep monitoring. Sara, hold on the clean cohort extraction until we have stable observed split for another hour.

Sara: will do. I'll also compute IPW-adjusted estimates as sensitivity check but won't use them for final decision unless we can't get clean assignment.

Jia: I'll scope the console SRM detector spec and share a PR by EOD.

Marco: PR for "observed split" badge in console opened: https://github.com/redwoodinc/console/pull/2891 — includes tooltip explaining how it's computed.

Samir: closing the ticket once data check is done.

Alex: thanks all. Summary: avoid promo for now, ops disabled fallback, eng adding observed split + detector, data will recompute significance on clean cohort or use bootstrap CIs. Re-evaluate in 48h or when variants hit target N. :thumbsup:
